text: Good evening. It is 6.03 p.m. on Thursday, November 14th. My name is Luke Wuttenwieser. I'm the Transportation Planner in the Transportation, Traffic, and Parking Department. This is a public hearing for the Government Center front sidewalk and plaza redesign. So just a little bit of background. I work in the Transportation, Traffic, and Parking Department, the mission of which is to ensure the safe and efficient movement of people and goods in the City of Stanford, really focusing on safety and accessibility for all users. And then just a little bit about Vision Zero. Stanford Vision Zero is a commitment to eliminate traffic deaths by 2032. We recognize that one death is too many, people make mistakes, people are vulnerable, safety is proactive, and we focus on reduced speeds. This project is, you know, part of our overall program that the Mayor has committed us to to improve safety and accessibility for all roadway users. So a little bit of background. The Government Center is located at 888 Washington Boulevard at the intersection of Tresor Boulevard and Washington Boulevard at the northwestern parcel on the corner of the intersection there. The original building was built in the mid-1980s, as well as the sidewalk and plaza. The sidewalk and plaza area are deteriorated sidewalks, as you can see here, significant cracking and heaving, as well as cross-slope issues on the sidewalk, rendering it, you know, difficult for those with mobility impairments to get by. There's certain crumbling infrastructure, such as around the, you know, as the sidewalk areas here, as you can see, drainage, as well as around the foundation and base of the building, a lot of also aesthetic issues, and then the building and the area is just, you know, kind of past its useful life at this point. That's a little bit of a background about the project. Project info. So the goals, first and foremost, is to improve accessibility and ADA compliance. There are several areas lacking in ADA compliance. Obviously, this was built pre-ADA, as well as just, you know, trip hazards and different things of that nature. So really, first and foremost, improving accessibility and ADA compliance, increasing green space as part of the Mayor's Executive Order for Environmental Sustainability, increasing public seating, creating a new kind of public plaza area, and, you know, really welcoming people to the Government Center, upgrading and hardening our infrastructure. So I mentioned before some infrastructure deficiencies, so we're going to upgrade our infrastructure, such as drainage, sidewalks, building facade measures, lighting, structural components of the building, the increasing lighting as well. There's currently no pedestrian lighting around the sidewalks on Washington or Tresor Boulevard, so improving lighting to improve safety. Details of the project is going to be completely new sidewalks along both frontages of the building, along Washington Boulevard and Tresor Boulevard, as well as kind of a new upper plaza patio area. So it's going to go new, basically all new material from the building face out to the curbside curb face. New street trees will be planted. We're only increasing the number of street trees throughout the project area to, you know, improve air quality and reduce the urban heat island effect. As mentioned before, new public seating areas really kind of, you know, create new spaces for people to kind of come and enjoy the government center and take part in commerce and business here at the government center. Expanding pollinator pathways and green space expansion, so there's several new planted areas, you know, that can support pollinators. And then also new lighting on the sidewalk, plaza, and around the building. So sidewalks are going to have pedestrian level lighting, plaza itself is going to have lighting, and then actually the building itself is going to have some nice decorative uplighting as well, really to improve visibility and safety in the whole area. And of course, new ADA compliant ramps and walkways, so new ADA compliant ways to get up into the building from the sidewalk, and the walkways and sidewalks themselves will be, you know, completely reconstructed to be ADA compliant. So it's all new sidewalks, all new plaza area, you know, new planters, new planted gardens, etc. And this is a three million dollar project that's funded by the state of Connecticut. So this is just a high level graphic design, as you can see here, so just to orient yourselves, this is Washington Boulevard going north, south, or up and down. This is Tresor Boulevard going left and right, east and west. Essentially, it's new 10-foot wide sidewalk, which is, you know, our city standard for width. New seating areas in within planted garden areas as well, you know, places for people to kind of sit, relax, and enjoy themselves. A new central front plaza, which will really be a new kind of new government plaza area for different events, flag racings, different things like that, press announcements, etc. Upgrading the bus shelter with a new bus shelter and seating areas for buses, and passengers waiting for the buses. We have over 75 people board the bus right in front of the government center every single day, so we want to make sure we have facilities built for them. And then also just, you know, everywhere in green you can see is kind of a new garden pollinator pathway area, and these are the ADA compliant ramps leading you up from the sidewalk up to the building. We also have a ramp near the Washington Boulevard garage entrance, as well as, you know, just upgrading sidewalks and lighting all throughout the project area. And then over here by the Tresor Boulevard exit area is a space that could be used for food trucks, you know, in the future as well. So upgrading all the new sidewalks, building completely new, upgrading lighting, new plaza area, and there's also new seating areas within. These are all street trees as well that you can see throughout the area, which really are also we're planting them in planted areas and planters, so there's proper soil volume for them so it can actually live, but also the roots aren't going to impact the sidewalks and cause tripping hazards like they do now. And then these are just some rendering. So this is standing out on Washington Boulevard looking from the street, looking towards the building in the front. You can see this new front plaza area over here, as well as some of the new street trees and street lights that'll be coming. This is still a draft rendering. This is not necessarily representative of the final design. Here's a look on aerial overhead. This is Tresor Boulevard right below here. You see the new bus stop and bus shelter, the new ramps, and also this new kind of front plaza area, and all the new trees that we're planting, really increasing green space from what is beyond today, as well as all the new pollinator pathways, planted gardens, to really enhance sustainability, stormwater capture, and also reducing the urban heat island effect as well. And this is from the Washington Boulevard side, very similar. New street trees, street lighting, access ways to increase porosity between the government center, upper plaza, as well as the sidewalk, as well as all those new planted areas. So really an emphasis on new trees, an expansion of trees, expansion of green space, to really make sure they're all, you know, supportive and grow. And also all the new seating areas as well. And then also there's new driveway, you know, the crosswalks by each driveway, it will also be redone as well. It's worth noting that the lane configuration is remaining the same, so it's not really an impact to traffic at this point. And this is just kind of a lower level, pedestrian level view of that front plaza area by the front of the government center building. And you can see the new ADA compliant ramps, really to improve wheelchair and access and those with mobility impairments up to the front doors of the government center. And then this is kind of just a wider birds out view as well, as you can see here. And a lot of these photos have also been placed down in the government center lobby as well, if you would like to take a look there. And thank you, that is it. This is my contact information, feel free to reach out if you have any questions. This meeting will be posted on the City's website as well for later viewing.
